title: The Inherited Country Learning to Return Itself

features.name: the property line dissolving
features.desc-on-touch: The fence that marked ownership has become a living thing. Roots run through both sides indifferently. The land has learned that divisions are only real if the ground agrees.

features.name: the deed that forgot itself
features.desc-on-touch: Somewhere the original deed is filed. But the land has outgrown the language in which it was written. The country now knows itself in terms the deed cannot contain.

features.name: the returning roots
features.desc-on-touch: They grow back toward their source, learning their own history as they descend. The country is remembering itself hand over hand, root over root.

features.name: the inherited grief
features.desc-on-touch: Something lives in the soil that remembers the original taking. The land holds no grudge but it remembers. The memory shapes what grows here.

features.name: the future already growing
features.desc-on-touch: This place is becoming itself. The trees that will stand here in fifty years are already deciding their shape. The country is writing its own return.
